title: Renewal conversation slate and deck protocol
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical playbook for running account-level quarterly reviews and renewal conversations across two reusable deck families: Compact (operational/renewal-focused) and Enterprise (strategic, exec+technical). The doc includes a slide-by-slide skeleton, speaker notes, a lightweight renewal-risk rubric, a renewal tracker template (text form), pre-meeting checklist, and two canned follow-up emails.

When to use each deck family:
- Compact Deck (20-30 min): use for SMB and mid-market accounts where the goal is alignment on usage, blockers, and a renewal check-in. Fast cadence, execution-focused.
- Standard Deck (45-60 min): core Customer Success QBR for typical accounts with some management present; covers adoption, roadmap, and success plan.
- Enterprise Deep Deck (75-90 min): for strategic accounts with technical stakeholders and exec sponsors; includes deep operational health, performance metrics, SLOs, integration roadmap, and renewal negotiation anchors.

Slide skeletons and speaker notes (reusable blocks):
1) Title / Meeting frame (1 slide)
   - Title: Account QBR — [Account name] | [Date]
   - Speaker note: 30s welcome, introduce attendees and objectives (align on health, risks, renewals, and next steps).

2) Executive snapshot (1 slide) — Compact & Enterprise
   - KPIs: ARR today, 90-day ARR movement, active product modules, NRR estimate.
   - Speaker note: 1-2 sentences on the account state and the primary ask of this QBR (e.g., alignment, escalation, renewal intent).

3) Usage and adoption (1-2 slides)
   - Metrics sample: daily active users (DAU), requests per min, tokens/month, peak latency percentile. Provide trends (90d vs 30d).
   - Speaker note: Highlight where usage is expanding or stalling; call out specific features driving value.

4) Value delivered / Success stories (1 slide)
   - Pull 2-3 concrete outcomes: e.g., feature X reduced processing time by 40%, embedding-driven search improved NPS by +6.
   - Speaker note: Ask the customer to confirm these wins; surface any missing context.

5) Technical health & risk (Enterprise only: 2-3 slides)
   - Items: latency and error SLOs, deployment topology (hosted/dedicated/private), incident history, security posture.
   - Speaker note: Be candid about known issues and mitigation plans. Map each risk to owner and ETA.

6) Commercial & renewal status (1 slide)
   - Current contract end date, committed ARR, pending PO, price band, and renewal timeline.
   - Speaker note: State where we are and what horizon matters for procurement.

7) Renewal risk rubric (1 slide)
   - Use a simple RAG score (Green/Amber/Red) across five dimensions: Product Value, Adoption, Technical Health, Exec Sponsorship, Procurement Readiness. Each dimension scored 1-5 and color-coded.
   - Example scoring: Product Value=4 (Green); Adoption=3 (Amber); Technical Health=2 (Red) -> Overall Amber.
   - Speaker note: Explain what needs to change to move colors.

8) Action plan & owners (1-2 slides)
   - 90-day plan with owners and checkpoints. Include the renewal ask (target + timing), upsell/cross-sell opportunities, and technical remediation tasks.
   - Speaker note: Confirm owners and commitments live in the meeting; capture dates.

9) Appendix & data sources (1+ slides)
   - Sources: product dashboards, support ticket links, evals, benchmark docs, audit logs.
   - Speaker note: Point reviewers to where they can drill into the metrics post-call.

Timing guidance by deck type (suggested):
- Compact: 5m intro, 6m snapshot, 6m adoption, 3m commercial, 5m actions -> 25m total.
- Standard: 5m intro, 8m snapshot, 12m adoption/value, 8m commercial/risk, 10m actions -> 43m total.
- Enterprise: 8m intro, 10m snapshot, 20m adoption/value, 15m technical deep dive, 12m commercial, 15m actions -> ~80m.

Renewal tracker (plaintext template) — one line per account:
- Account: [name] | AE: [name] | CS: [name] | ARR: [$] | Contract end: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Renewal status: [Green/Amber/Red] | Next step: [e.g., 'schedule renewal sync'] | Owner: [name] | Last contact: [YYYY-MM-DD] | Open issues: [short list]

Scoring notes and cutoffs (suggested):
- Green: score >= 4 on at least 4/5 dims and no single dim <=2.
- Amber: mixed scores, at least one 2 and one 3.
- Red: any dim at 1 or two dims at 2.

Pre-meeting checklist (owner: CS manager or assigned CSM)
- Verify contract dates and seats/units in billing system.
- Pull last 90-day usage trends and anomalies.
- Run the renewal risk rubric and draft recommended risk color.
- Confirm attendees (include procurement or technical leads for Enterprise).
- Share pre-read 48 hours before meeting with suggested agenda and questions.
- Open JIRA for technical follow-ups if needed (reference in appendix).

Field play: how to surface an unexpected red item during the QBR
- Acknowledge, record owner and ETA, propose temporary mitigation (e.g., fallback model, increased capacity), and commit to a follow-up checkpoint within 7 business days. Escalate to SRE/Platform if incident or risk impacts SLA.

Post-meeting follow-up templates (two short emails)
1) Short executive summary (to exec sponsor + internal AE)
   Subject: [Account] QBR — key outcomes & renewal next steps
   Body: Thanks for joining — bullets: 1) Overall status (Green/Amber/Red) + one-line rationale; 2) Top 3 actions with owners and due dates; 3) Renewal ask and next milestone; 4) Link to full deck and tracker.

2) Technical follow-up (to technical contacts)
   Subject: [Account] QBR — technical action items
   Body: Summary of technical items, links to logs/dashboards, proposed remediation steps, owner assignments, and suggested date for technical checkpoint.

Sample quick math for executive snapshot (to avoid confusion in meeting):
- ARR movement example: If current committed ARR = $450k and three upsell opportunities worth $50k are in pipeline with 60% CPT (confidence), expected ARR = 450k + (50k * 0.6) = $480k. Show conservative and upside scenarios.

Customization notes and do's/don'ts:
- Do keep executive slides to clear numbers and 1-2 visuals.
- Don't overload the slide deck with raw logs; put heavy data in appendix.
- Do standardize the renewal rubric across CSMs for consistent scoring.
- Don't promise discounts in the QBR — route pricing asks to AE/Commercial ops unless pre-approved.

Quick checklist for meeting artifacts to attach to Drive after the call:
- Final deck (PDF)
- Updated renewal tracker line and timestamp
- Action item list exported to JIRA or Linear with owners and due dates
- Link to relevant dashboard slices and support ticket threads

Suggested metrics to instrument consistently (column names for the tracker backend):
- account_id, account_name, cs_owner, ae_owner, arr, contract_end, last_success_story_date, active_users_30d, token_volume_30d, avg_latency_p95, error_rate_30d, renewal_score, renewal_color, next_step, next_step_owner, next_step_due_date, last_contact

Open questions for the team (items to iterate in next week):
- Should we introduce a 6-week pre-renewal cadence for accounts scoring Amber? (pros/cons)
- What weight should we give executive sponsorship in automated renewal scoring?
- Do we want a single canonical pre-read template or small variants per persona?

Notes on distribution and tooling:
- Put finalized family decks in the shared drive folder "customer-success/deck-templates" with naming: [account-size]-qbr-[compact|standard|enterprise]-v1.pdf.
- Renewal tracker should live in the shared tracker sheet (linked_artifacts above) and be exported to CRM weekly.

Appendix: quick sample slide copy (compact slide example)
- Title: QBR Snapshot — Acme Corp (Mar 2026)
- Bullets: 1) ARR: $420k (+5% Q/Q) 2) Key wins: Search latency down 38% after config change 3) Risk: Integration test failures blocking batch scoring (Owner: Diego) 4) Ask: Confirm procurement timeline and PO owner.

Author note: This file is intentionally compact and designed to be a working document. Expect iterative updates from the CS playbook working group; please add feedback in-line or push PR notes into the shared Slack thread.
